title: Tonic Immobility and Peritraumatic Dissociation as Risk Factors for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: A Systematic Review and Narrative Synthesis
abstract: Tonic immobility (TI) and peritraumatic dissociation (PTD) are involuntary peritraumatic responses associated with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following sexual assault. To our knowledge, no systematic review has concurrently examined both as distinct exposures in this population. To examine associations between TI and PTD with PTSD outcomes in adult survivors of sexual assault and interpersonal trauma. Studies were eligible if they included adult survivors of interpersonal trauma, directly measured TI or PTD, and reported PTSD-related outcomes. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 (PRISMA 2020) and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed and Google Scholar (inception to April 2026) was supplemented by hand-searching. Sixteen studies (total baseline N = 6,259; effective analysis N = 6,150) were included. Narrative synthesis with vote counting was performed due to effect-size heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Across 16 studies yielding 17 PTSD-specific comparisons, significant positive associations were found in 14 of 17 (82.4%). TI showed positive associations in 10 of 13 comparisons (76.9%), including a prospective OR = 2.75 (95% CI [1.50, 5.03]). All four studies examining PTD reported positive associations with PTSD outcomes, although the evidence base remains limited ( k = 4). Standardized effect sizes ranged from small (β ≈ .21) to large (β = .64), with most estimates falling in the small-to-medium range. Both TI and PTD are positively associated with PTSD following interpersonal trauma. Peritraumatic responses may have potential utility for early clinical risk assessment, although prospective validation is needed before routine implementation. Future research should address geographic diversity to establish cross-cultural generalizability.
